# AI Hub

> AI Hub is a self-hosted control plane that connects applications to private, OpenAI-compatible language models through outbound-only workers.

Canonical origin: https://aihub.mohsal.dev
Human documentation: https://aihub.mohsal.dev/docs
Source and detailed protocol documentation: https://github.com/mohsalsaleem/ai-hub

## Choose an integration

- Use the OpenAI-compatible API for text chat and response integrations.
- Use the native job API for durable, schema-validated structured generation.
- MCP is planned but is not currently exposed.
- Workers perform model inference only. They do not execute tools, uploaded code, or arbitrary application logic.

## Authentication

Create an application in the AI Hub console and copy its application token when shown. Send it as:

Authorization: Bearer aih_...

Application tokens can access only their own model profiles, task definitions, and runs. Keep tokens out of source control. Production requests must use HTTPS.

## OpenAI-compatible API

Base URL: https://aihub.mohsal.dev/v1

- GET /v1/models — list active chat model profiles for the authenticated application.
- POST /v1/chat/completions — create a synchronous, non-streaming text completion.
- POST /v1/responses — create a synchronous response, or set `background: true` for a durable asynchronous response.
- GET /v1/responses/:id — retrieve a durable response using the same application token.

Model IDs are immutable application-scoped task references such as `assistant.general@1`. A request may omit `@version` to select the latest active version belonging to that application.

Supported inputs are text `system`, `developer`, `user`, and `assistant` messages. Supported inference options are `temperature`, `top_p`, `stop`, and token limits. Responses also accept a top-level `instructions` string.

Streaming, tool calls, images, files, audio, embeddings, conversation objects, and `previous_response_id` are not supported. Streaming requests fail explicitly.

Synchronous calls wait for a worker for up to 60 seconds by default. A timed-out Chat Completions request returns HTTP 504 and includes the durable job ID; the job continues running. A synchronous Responses request that is still running returns HTTP 200 with `status: "in_progress"` and can be retrieved later by ID.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header when retrying a create request. Reusing it with identical parameters returns the original job. Reusing it with different parameters returns HTTP 409 with code `idempotency_conflict`.

## Native job API

Base URL: https://aihub.mohsal.dev/api/v1

- POST /api/v1/task_definitions — publish an immutable structured task definition.
- GET /api/v1/task_definitions — list the application's definitions.
- POST /api/v1/jobs — submit a durable job with a task reference, idempotency key, and JSON input.
- GET /api/v1/jobs/:id — retrieve job state and output.

Job states are `queued`, `leased`, `completed`, `failed`, and `dead`. The first two are non-terminal. Applications should poll until a terminal state and apply completed output idempotently because execution is at least once.

## Task definitions

A task definition is an immutable, application-scoped contract between an application and a worker. It fixes the instructions, executor, input schema, output schema, and required worker capabilities for every run using that definition.

Required fields for `POST /api/v1/task_definitions`:

- `key` — 3 to 100 characters; starts with a lowercase letter and then uses lowercase letters, numbers, `_`, `.`, or `-`.
- `version` — a positive integer, unique for the key inside the application.
- `executor` — `structured_generation` or `chat_completion`; defaults to `structured_generation`.
- `instructions` — non-empty model instructions, up to 20,000 characters.
- `input_schema` — a valid JSON Schema describing accepted job input.
- `output_schema` — a valid JSON Schema describing the worker's required output.
- `requirements` — optional object whose truthy keys are worker capabilities required for routing.

Example structured definition:

```json
{
  "task_definition": {
    "key": "document.summarize",
    "version": 1,
    "executor": "structured_generation",
    "instructions": "Summarize the supplied text without inventing facts.",
    "input_schema": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": ["text"],
      "properties": {"text": {"type": "string"}}
    },
    "output_schema": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": ["summary"],
      "properties": {"summary": {"type": "string"}}
    },
    "requirements": {"json_schema": true}
  }
}
```

The create response includes the canonical `reference`, such as `document.summarize@1`, and a SHA-256 `digest`. Submit a run using that exact reference:

```json
{
  "task": "document.summarize@1",
  "idempotency_key": "summary-order-4815",
  "input": {"text": "Text to summarize"}
}
```

The Hub validates job input before queueing and validates worker output before completion. A worker must advertise the executor and every required capability before it can claim the run.

Definitions cannot be edited after publication. When instructions, schemas, executor, or requirements change, publish the same key with a new version and update callers deliberately. Existing runs remain bound to their original version and digest.

For `chat_completion`, AI Hub supplies its standard chat input and output schemas when they are omitted. Chat definitions appear as models through `/v1/models`; their task reference is also their OpenAI-compatible model ID.

## Routing and privacy

Applications select an allowed worker pool and minimum worker trust level, never an individual worker. A cross-organization run requires an approved provider-owned shared pool, an explicit consumer grant, provider participation, compatible capabilities, and accepted trust.

Consumer APIs expose the selected pool and a general routing explanation but never worker, machine, provider-model, or provider-organization identity. The Hub and the selected worker necessarily receive plaintext request input and output.

## Metering and credits

Each claim attempt creates immutable execution evidence. Successful shared executions with provider-reported usage charge one internal credit per token. The provider receives 80% and AI Hub receives 20%, using integer accounting with the provider receiving any rounding remainder.

Failed attempts, expired leases, private runs, and executions without reported usage are uncharged. Platform operators can post positive or negative organization adjustments, but cannot edit existing entries. Adjustments require a reason and record the operator in an immutable audit event. Credits are internal accounting units; payments, transfers, cash conversion, and payouts are not enabled.

## Limits and failure handling

- Job request and result payloads are limited to 256 KiB.
- Task-definition API requests are limited to 96 KiB.
- Workers use 180-second renewable leases and bounded retries.
- Use a background Responses request for work that may exceed an HTTP timeout.
- Preserve returned job IDs for recovery and support.
